title: India Won by an Innings and 300 Runs. It Is Their Biggest Test Victory in History.
excerpt: Manav Suthar took 6-33 on debut, Washington Sundar claimed 4-36 in the second innings, and a 564-run declaration left Afghanistan with nowhere to hide at Mullanpur.
body:
## India Won by an Innings and 300 Runs. It Is Their Biggest Test Victory in History.

India did not need a fourth day. They did not even need a full third day.

At the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur on Monday, Shubman Gill's side completed the most emphatic Test victory in Indian cricket history — an innings and 300 runs against Afghanistan, surpassing the previous record of an innings and 262 runs against the same opposition in Bengaluru in 2018.

The match lasted just over two and a half days. India batted once, scored 564 for 8 declared, and bowled Afghanistan out twice — for 152 and 112 — inside the equivalent of a single day's play.

## Suthar's debut for the ages

The headlines from this match will belong, deservedly, to Manav Suthar. The 23-year-old left-arm spinner from Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, making his Test debut, returned figures of 6 for 33 in Afghanistan's first innings — the third-best figures by an Indian spinner on debut, behind only Narendra Hirwani's legendary 8-61 and 8-75 against the West Indies in 1988.

Suthar bowled 22 overs, 10 of them maidens, at an economy rate of 1.50. He dismissed Abdul Malik, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Afsar Zazai, and then completed his five-wicket haul by bowling first-innings top-scorer Rahmat Shah for 60 before trapping Mohammad Saleem lbw three balls later. The stadium erupted. Social media followed.

Ravichandran Ashwin, who retired from international cricket last year, was among the first to congratulate Suthar. "Manav Suthar. Best wishes for a wonderful career ahead," he wrote on X. Chennai Super Kings, Lucknow Super Giants, and a cascade of cricket accounts echoed the sentiment.

For Indian fans abroad, Suthar's debut is a source of pride, showcasing the depth of talent emerging from India. NRI fans took to social media to express their excitement, with many highlighting how this new generation of players could inspire future cricketing stars in their communities.

## Sundar seals it in the second innings

If Suthar owned the first innings, Washington Sundar owned the second. The off-spinning all-rounder, who had already contributed 52 not out with the bat in India's declaration total, took 4 for 36 as Afghanistan crumbled to 112 all out following on.

Afghanistan's second innings lasted 37.4 overs. With the pitch deteriorating and India's spinners extracting sharp turn, no Afghan batter managed to cross 40. Sediqullah Atal's 33 was the highest individual score. Sharafuddin Ashraf, nursing a quad injury from India's innings, did not bat.

Mohammed Siraj provided the initial breakthrough in the second innings before Kuldeep Yadav chipped in with a wicket — captain Gill's tactical field placement at long-on tricking Rahmanullah Gurbaz into a risky aerial strike. Prasidh Krishna, who had taken 3-37 in the first innings, kept the pressure tight from the other end.

## The batting mountain Afghanistan never climbed

India's first-innings total of 564 for 8 declared was constructed on centuries from captain Gill (126) and KL Rahul (100), along with commanding half-centuries from Sai Sudharsan (81), Rishabh Pant (81), and Sundar (52 not out). Mohammad Saleem's 6-wicket haul was a spirited effort for Afghanistan — the 23-year-old completed a career-best return in just his second Test — but the visitors were always chasing shadows.

Rahul's century was his 12th in Tests, punctuated by a special celebration dedicated to his daughter Evaarah. Gill, in his growing tenure as captain, became the second-fastest Indian skipper to 1,000 Test runs, behind only Sunil Gavaskar.

## A record that speaks for itself

The margin of an innings and 300 runs is India's largest ever in Test cricket, eclipsing the innings-and-262-run defeat of Afghanistan in their 2018 Test debut at Bengaluru. It is also among the largest victories in the history of Test cricket.

For the NRI community watching from abroad, the match offered a showcase of India's next generation. Suthar, Sundar, Sudharsan — the names that will define Indian cricket in the years ahead stepped up in a match where established stars like Kohli and Rohit were absent. Many fans expressed their hopes that these young players would continue to excel, fostering a stronger connection with their roots and inspiring future generations in their adopted countries.

India's attention now turns to the three-match ODI series against Afghanistan, starting June 13 in Dharamshala, where Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma return to action. The white-ball contests promise a different challenge for both sides.

*Sources: Reuters, CricketTimes, Wikipedia*
